text:
Utah beat Columbus 4-1 on the scoreboard and lost the game on the shot-quality ledger. Columbus generated 3.00 expected goals to Utah's 2.66, and at even strength the gap was wide: 2.70 to 1.53. Run the chances through a thousand replays and the Blue Jackets win 56 percent of them. They lost this one because three of Utah's four goals came with the man advantage, where the Blue Jackets' penalty kill gave up 3 of 4 chances while their own power play never got going (0 for 2).

Utah's first period was the cleanest hockey on either side. The Mammoth outchanced Columbus 0.72 to 0.15 in expected goals, and Mikhail Sergachev's slap shot on the power play at 11:55 opened the scoring, followed by Nick Schmaltz's snap shot at 16:31 for a 2-0 lead. Kent Johnson pulled one back 1:30 into the second, and from there Columbus owned the territory, outchancing Utah 1.20 to 0.68 in the second and 1.65 to 1.25 in the third.

The difference was in the nets. Sebastian Cossa faced 3.00 expected goals and allowed one, saving two goals more than an average goalie would have. Jet Greaves was a shade below expectation, and Dylan Guenther (a goal and two assists) and Schmaltz (two goals on eight shots) both cashed in on the power play in the third, at 5:59 and 14:13. Columbus spent two periods pressing and had one goal to show for it.
